standardSteps.name: outline
standardSteps.narration: A rectangle measuring twenty-three by fourteen has area twenty-three groups of fourteen. We will prove that by splitting the sides.
standardSteps.prompt: What does the area of the full rectangle represent?

standardSteps.name: partition
standardSteps.narration: Split twenty-three into twenty and three. Split fourteen into ten and four. Every part of both original side lengths is still present.
standardSteps.prompt: Why must each side add back to its original length?

standardSteps.name: part-1
standardSteps.narration: Twenty times ten makes two hundred in the top-left region. That is the first partial product.
standardSteps.prompt: Why is this part two hundred?

standardSteps.name: part-2
standardSteps.narration: Three times ten makes thirty in the top-right region. This width is three, not twenty-three.
standardSteps.prompt: Which two side parts made thirty?

standardSteps.name: part-3
standardSteps.narration: Twenty times four makes eighty in the bottom-left region. We have not lost the four units from the height.
standardSteps.prompt: Where does the eighty come from?

standardSteps.name: part-4
standardSteps.narration: Three times four makes twelve in the bottom-right. All four parts now fill the original rectangle.
standardSteps.prompt: Have we counted every region exactly once?

standardSteps.name: partials
standardSteps.narration: Add two hundred, thirty, eighty and twelve. Every partial product is area, so the sum is the whole area.
standardSteps.prompt: How does addition rebuild the whole rectangle?

standardSteps.name: total
standardSteps.narration: Two hundred plus thirty plus eighty plus twelve is three hundred and twenty-two. So twenty-three times fourteen is three hundred and twenty-two.
standardSteps.prompt: How do you know no part was missed?

steps.name: Inspect the expression
steps.narration: An x squared tile, six x rods and five units represent x squared plus six x plus five. Can they make a perfect square?
steps.prompt: Which tiles already make a square?

steps.name: Split the x rods
steps.narration: Six x rods split evenly into two groups of three. We will place three rods along each side of the x squared tile.
steps.prompt: Why is half of six equal to three?

steps.name: Build the lower edge
steps.narration: Three x rods extend the bottom side. The new width is x plus three.
steps.prompt: What length did we add?

steps.name: Build the right edge
steps.narration: The other three x rods extend the right side. Both outer edges now measure x plus three.
steps.prompt: What shape will fill the remaining corner?

steps.name: Find the missing corner

steps.prompt: How many extra squares complete the corner?

steps.name: Complete the corner

steps.prompt: Did those four extra units exist in the original expression?

steps.name: Read the two equal edges
steps.narration: Each edge is x plus three, so the completed area is the square of x plus three.
steps.prompt: How can you tell this really is a square?

steps.name: Meet the two pans
steps.narration: A mystery bag has value x. Unit weights each have a value of one. Watch what happens when we build a balanced equation.
steps.prompt: What does the x bag stand for?

steps.name: Load the left pan
steps.narration: Put the x bag and three unit weights onto the left. The balance tips because the right pan is still empty.
steps.prompt: Is it equal yet?

steps.name: Load the right pan

steps.prompt: What makes the two sides equal?

steps.name: Remove one from both

steps.prompt: Why not take one weight from only the left?

steps.name: Remove two more from both
steps.narration: Remove two more weights from each pan. Only x remains on the left and four weights remain on the right.
steps.prompt: What is x now?

steps.narration: The unknown x is four. Check it by replacing the x bag with four units: four plus three equals seven.
steps.prompt: How can you check your answer?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Load signed weights
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Two mystery bags and three negative unit balloons sit on the left. A negative balloon pulls upwards. The left side represents two x minus three.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: How does a negative balloon change the total?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Balance both pans
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: One mystery bag and two positive units sit on the right. Both sides represent equal values: two x minus three equals x plus two.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: What must x be to balance these signed pans?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Remove x from both
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Remove one x bag from both pans. Because the same thing was removed twice, the equation stays equal. One x minus three equals two.

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Add three to both
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Add three positive units to each pan. On the left, each positive unit and negative balloon forms a zero pair. Three zero pairs are worth nothing.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: Why does a positive one and a negative one cancel?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Cancel the zero pairs
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Remove the three zero pairs from the left. Nothing changes in value: the positive and negative units cancel. The left pan now has only x; the right pan holds five units.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: What value is left for x?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Check with substitution

SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: How do both sides give seven?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Reveal the mystery cups
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Each covered cup hides the same unknown number of counters. We call that value x. The divider says both sides have equal total value.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: What does every mystery cup represent?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Build the equality
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Two mystery cups and two loose counters on the left have the same value as ten counters on the right. We write two x plus two equals ten.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Why do two cups mean two x?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Remove two from each side
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Remove the two loose counters from the left and exactly two from the right. Both sides lose the same value, so they remain equal.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: How many counters remain on the right?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Match one pile to each cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Two x equals eight. Split the eight counters into two equal groups, one group for each cup. The groups must be the same size.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: How many counters belong in each equal group?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Fill the first cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Place four counters into the first mystery cup, using the four counters from the right side. Four more remain for the second cup.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Does each cup have to hold the same number?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Fill the second cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: The final four counters belong to the second cup. Both cups now contain four: x equals four.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: What value does x have?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Check by substitution
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Replace each cup with four counters. Two groups of four plus two makes ten, the same as the ten counters on the right. The solution is correct.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Can you check the equation using four?

SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: How does a negative balloon change the total?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Balance both pans
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: One mystery bag and two positive units sit on the right. Both sides represent equal values: two x minus three equals x plus two.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: What must x be to balance these signed pans?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Remove x from both
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Remove one x bag from both pans. Because the same thing was removed twice, the equation stays equal. One x minus three equals two.

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Add three to both
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Add three positive units to each pan. On the left, each positive unit and negative balloon forms a zero pair. Three zero pairs are worth nothing.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: Why does a positive one and a negative one cancel?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Cancel the zero pairs
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Remove the three zero pairs from the left. Nothing changes in value: the positive and negative units cancel. The left pan now has only x; the right pan holds five units.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: What value is left for x?

SIGNED_STEPS.name: Check with substitution
SIGNED_STEPS.narration: Replace x with five. Two times five minus three equals seven, and five plus two equals seven. Both pans balance.
SIGNED_STEPS.prompt: How do both sides give seven?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Reveal the mystery cups
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Each covered cup hides the same unknown number of counters. We call that value x. The divider says both sides have equal total value.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: What does every mystery cup represent?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Build the equality
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Two mystery cups and two loose counters on the left have the same value as ten counters on the right. We write two x plus two equals ten.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Why do two cups mean two x?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Remove two from each side
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Remove the two loose counters from the left and exactly two from the right. Both sides lose the same value, so they remain equal.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: How many counters remain on the right?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Match one pile to each cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Two x equals eight. Split the eight counters into two equal groups, one group for each cup. The groups must be the same size.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: How many counters belong in each equal group?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Fill the first cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Place four counters into the first mystery cup, using the four counters from the right side. Four more remain for the second cup.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Does each cup have to hold the same number?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Fill the second cup
CUPS_STEPS.narration: The final four counters belong to the second cup. Both cups now contain four: x equals four.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: What value does x have?

CUPS_STEPS.name: Check by substitution
CUPS_STEPS.narration: Replace each cup with four counters. Two groups of four plus two makes ten, the same as the ten counters on the right. The solution is correct.
CUPS_STEPS.prompt: Can you check the equation using four?
